mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous surge in earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 6% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the GDP decline is reversed within two quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 for four consecutive months signals labor market strength that boosts corporate profit margins and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by at least 100,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero during triggered periods, or the employment trend reverses within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the decline in industrial production reverses within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% month-over-month signals strong housing demand and inflationary pressure, which increases interest rate expectations and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises >3% MoM AND CPIAUCSL rises >3% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the inflation spike is transitory and reverts within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 2% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy that supports risk asset valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for >6 months AND CPIAUCSL < 3% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly above the median of all periods, or inflation exceeds 3% YoY before the horizon ends.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% combined with accelerating wage growth (implied by PAYEMS growth outpacing labor force expansion) signals labor market overheating, which increases cost pressures and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate tighter Fed policy.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS growth outpaces labor force growth for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or wage growth decelerates before policy response occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the decline in retail sales reverses within two months.
